paper_title: Thermal-Aware Task Mapping on Dynamically Reconfigurable Network-on-Chip Based Multiprocessor System-on-Chip

extraction.paper_title: Thermal-Aware Task Mapping on Dynamically Reconfigurable Network-on-Chip Based Multiprocessor System-on-Chip

scenario.figure_or_table: Fig. 1 (motivational example) with Fig. 2/Fig. 3/Fig. 18 as related thermal-map results
scenario.description: Steady-state HotSpot thermal maps of six dark-silicon activation patterns (50% dark cores) on an 8x8 Alpha 21264 core array at 22 nm, all running the same multi-thread H.264 workload at full voltage/frequency. Reported observable is per-pattern chip peak temperature in degrees C: pattern 1 80.67, pattern 2 82.17, pattern 3 82.15, pattern 4 75.67, pattern 5 80.11, pattern 6 72.81. The safe threshold is Tsafe = 81.8 C. The paper does not publish per-core x/y/width/height coordinates or per-core wattage for this scenario, and no pinned assets are supplied.
scenario.architecture: 8x8 homogeneous Alpha 21264 core array, 22 nm, 2.6 GHz, 64GB memory, mesh NoC (the paper's broader work targets SMART NoC); core power from McPAT, thermal from HotSpot v5.02
scenario.workload: Multi-thread H.264 application executed on active cores at full voltage/frequency; 50% of cores dark; dark core power assumed zero
scenario.operating_point: Steady state after a period of computation; 2.6 GHz; ambient 318.15 K (45 C); threshold 354.95 K (81.8 C); chip peak temperature per pattern in C (Fig. 1 labels)

original_setup.solver: HotSpot v5.02 in grid model mode for steady-state thermal maps, with per-core power from McPAT at 22 nm. MatEx is used for transient and peak temperature at runtime in task mapping decisions (PDF pages 4 and 12).
original_setup.optimizer: ILP model for optimal task mapping and scheduling, plus the polynomial-time heuristic TopoMap (Algorithms 1-3). Fig. 1 is a motivational comparison of six hand-chosen dark-silicon activation patterns and does not use these optimizers (PDF pages 2, 4, 9-11).
original_setup.controller: No closed-loop thermal controller. Runtime thermal-aware task mapping keeps temperature below Tsafe = 81.8 C by activating decentralized cores and powering off cores within one hop of active cores, on a reconfigurable SMART NoC with single-cycle multi-hop bypass, HPCmax = 8 (PDF pages 5, 6 and 12). Fig. 1 itself uses fixed activation patterns at full voltage/frequency with no controller.
original_setup.benchmark: Fig. 1 motivational example: multi-thread H.264 on an 8x8 Alpha 21264 core array, 22 nm, 2.6 GHz, 50% dark cores, six activation patterns (PDF page 4). The paper's evaluation benchmarks are PARSEC (Blackscholes, Facesim, Vips, Swaptions), X264 and DSP-stone, on 4x4, 6x6, 8x8 and 10x10 SMART NoCs (PDF pages 10-12).

thermal_observable.location: Chip peak temperature of the 8x8 core array, read from the Fig. 1 pattern labels. Pattern 1 80.67, pattern 2 82.17, pattern 3 82.15, pattern 4 75.67, pattern 5 80.11, pattern 6 72.81. No single scenario value is selected because the observable is reported per pattern.
thermal_observable.aggregation: Steady-state chip peak (maximum over the core array) after a period of computation, one value per activation pattern. The paper also reports 6.5 C and 9.3 C reductions relative to contiguous patterns.

physical_mismatches.reason: Not a 3D, interposer or chiplet stack. The scenario is a monolithic 2D homogeneous core array, so interposer, 3D and chiplet-floorplan thermal effects are not represented.

The paper's optimizer (ILP/TopoMap task mapping on a SMART NoC with bypass routing) and runtime MatEx transient control are not part of the Fig. 1 steady-state HotSpot scenario, so optimizer and controller behavior cannot be reproduced from it.

No per-core x/y/width/height geometry and no per-core wattage are published. Only the array size (8x8), the 50% dark fraction and peak temperatures are given, so floorplan and power inputs cannot be reconstructed.

The cooling and package model is given only partially in Table 2 (HotSpot parameters). Chip thickness 0.15 mm, heat sink convection resistance 0.1 K/W and ambient 318.15 K are listed. Die dimensions, spreader and sink geometry, and package layers are not given, which limits solver fidelity.
Pattern-specific active-core locations are shown only graphically in Fig. 1. They are not tabulated and would have to be digitized with uncertainty.
Reliability is addressed only through the Tsafe = 81.8 C threshold. There is no lifetime or electromigration model.

studio_assumptions: No pinned assets or code are supplied, so any Studio package would use its own bundled 2D steady-state thermal solver and default material and package properties, which are not the paper's HotSpot v5.02 grid model.

The only paper-published thermal inputs usable as Studio assumptions are the Table 2 values: silicon conductivity 100 W/m-K, chip thickness 0.15 mm, spreader conductivity 400 W/m-K, and ambient 318.15 K (45 C).

code.note: No repository, supplementary code, or pinned assets exist. All 17 pages show only DOI/handle links (p.1), which are bibliographic. The paper gives no HotSpot config, McPAT config, or scripts, so nothing is executable.

parameters.note: Table 2 values (0.15 mm, 100 W/m-K, 400 W/m-K, 0.1 K/W, 140.4 J/K, 318.15/354.95 K) match PDF p.12. The Table 2 values are not confirmed as the settings used for Fig. 1.

data.note: The six peak values were read from pdftotext layout output of Fig. 1, not from the rendered figure. The gate failed because the custom 2D steady experiment has an empty floorplan and no power_w object, so the input is invalid (input_gate_pass=false, scientific_gate_pass=false, independently_verified=false). comparison_valid=false. The scenario is the Fig. 1 motivational example: an 8x8 Alpha 21264 array at 22 nm, 2.6 GHz, 50% dark cores, running multi-thread H.264 in steady state with HotSpot v5.02 and McPAT power. The paper reports per-pattern chip peaks of 80.67, 82.17, 82.15, 75.67, 80.11 and 72.81 C against Tsafe = 81.8 C. Patterns 2 and 3 exceed the threshold, and the uniform pattern 6 is lowest. These are paper-reported values only, not reproduced. Since no simulation ran, there is no Studio temperature, no transient trace (this is a steady-state request) and no numerical comparison with the paper. Qualitatively, the paper reports that spreading active cores apart, so each is surrounded by dark cores, lowers the peak versus contiguous activation. This is the paper's own finding and was not checked here. No pinned assets exist (no Ascend910 or ATPlace commit, no generated placement and no input.flp or input.ptrace), so there is no source commit or placement assumption to report. The result must not be read as an exact replication or validation of the paper.
